C0.quote: assess qualities of various multiwinner election rules
C0.note: Multiwinner election rules evaluated by distortion and simulations.

C1.quote: we assess the worst-case loss of utility of multiwinner rules
C1.note: Distortion theorems and simulations of average utility. Axiomatic or strategic analysis is absent.

C2.1.value: preferences of the voters over the candidates (preference rankings)
C2.1.quote: preference relation of vi, which is a linear order over C

C2.2.quote: which is a linear order over C

C2.3.quote: indicating her preferences over the issues
C2.3.note: Voters hold binary preferred outcomes on issues.

C2.4.quote: each instance of indirect elections can be interpreted as a simple election
C2.4.note: The ranking is derived from the issue preferences and the rules are applied directly. There is no talk of misreporting.

C3.2.note: The ranking is defined as consistent with issue preferences by the model, but sincere submission is not stated.

C4.1.quote: voter v ranks the candidates according to the number of issues
C4.1.note: The ranking is generated from the issue-agreement model, and utility is defined as the number of issues on which the committee agrees with the voter.

C5.1.quote: define the utility of the voter vi from a committee W
C5.1.note: Utilitarian and Nash welfare, and distortion.

C5.2.quote: comparing those decisions to the preferred outcomes of the voters
C5.2.note: Utility is evaluated on issue preferences, which are separate from the rankings.

VOT.note: Voters take no modelled action beyond their fixed rankings.

OTH.note: The elected committee decides by majority but is not a strategic agent; its behaviour is fixed.
